subject: Looking under the hood of the indProd function

messages.author: bec3b6c763e426c0
messages.subject: Looking under the hood of the indProd function
parts:
I am trying to look under the hood of the indProd function for modelling interactions to understand how it works. Specifically, I am using the "orthogonalize" function, which uses a residual-centered indicators products (Little et al. 2006). However, the results I get from the "orthogonalize" function (see method 2 below) are not consistent with the results of the manual (step-by-step) method (see method 1 below). The strange thing is that the results of the two methods match if Z (the moderating LV) has three indicators. 
In the script below (where method 1 and 2 produce inconsistent results), Z is measured by a single indicator, Z1. The other LV that creates the product term is X and it is measured by X1, X2, and X3. 
Could someone explain this discrepancy? 
Thanks. 

Here is the code I used, which reproduces the problem : 

myData <- data.frame(replicate(7,sample(1:7,10,rep=TRUE)))
colnames(myData) = c("X1","X2","X3","Z1","Y1","Y2","Y3")
myData

### Method 1 (manual, step-by-step method to create residual-centered product terms): 
##Step 1a: Form Product Terms
myData$X1Z1 <- myData$X1 * myData$Z1
myData$X2Z1 <- myData$X2 * myData$Z1
myData$X3Z1 <- myData$X3 * myData$Z1

##Step 1b: Regress Product Terms on Predictors
#Product term 1: 
reg_X1Z1 <- lm(X1Z1 ~ X1 + X2 + X3 + Z1, data = myData)
summary(reg_X1Z1)
myData$X1Z1_o <- resid(reg_X1Z1) #Add resid to data frame

#Product term 2: 
reg_X2Z1 <- lm(X2Z1 ~ X1 + X2 + X3 + Z1, data = myData)
summary(reg_X2Z1)
myData$X2Z1_o <- resid(reg_X2Z1) #Add resid to data frame

#Product term 3: 
reg_X3Z1 <- lm(X3Z1 ~ X1 + X2 + X3 + Z1, data = myData)
summary(reg_X3Z1)
myData$X3Z1_o <- resid(reg_X3Z1) #Add resid to data frame

### Method 2 (automated method to create residual-centered product terms): 
myData2 <- orthogonalize(myData, var1 = c("X1","X2","X3"), var2="Z1", 
                         var3 = NULL, match = F, namesProd = NULL)

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: Looking under the hood of the indProd function
parts:
Thanks for catching this. It's certainly odd and I've been investigating it for a bit. I think you might be seeing some differences due to the nature of the data you've been generating (data where all the variables are not correlated with one another and means are not equal to 0). In your example though, the relationship between the orthogonalized terms and the outcome is the same for the variables created manually and by indProd:

##Running this should give you the same slope/se for the orthogonalized terms:
summary(lm(Y1 ~ X1 + X2 + X3 + Z1 + X1Z1_o, data = myData2))
summary(lm(Y1 ~ X1 + X2 + X3 + Z1 + X1.Z1, data = myData2))

And if you try this with a different data set you see the results are the same in the SEM model (using an example data set in the semTools package):


library(semTools)
library(lavaan)

dat2wayRC <- orthogonalize(dat2way, 1:3, 4, match = FALSE)

model1 <- "
f1 =~ x1 + x2 + x3
f2 =~ x4
f12 =~ x1.x4 + x2.x4 + x3.x4
f3 =~ x7 + x8 + x9
f3 ~ f1 + f2 + f12
"

fitRC2way <- sem(model1, data = dat2wayRC, std.lv = FALSE,
                 meanstructure = TRUE)
summary(fitRC2way)

## Residual center by hand

dat2wayRC$x1x4 <- dat2wayRC$x1*dat2wayRC$x4
dat2wayRC$x2x4 <- dat2wayRC$x2*dat2wayRC$x4
dat2wayRC$x3x4 <- dat2wayRC$x3*dat2wayRC$x4

dat2wayRC$x1x4o <- resid(lm(x1x4~x1+x2+x3+x4, data = dat2wayRC))
dat2wayRC$x2x4o <- resid(lm(x2x4~x1+x2+x3+x4, data = dat2wayRC))
dat2wayRC$x3x4o <- resid(lm(x3x4~x1+x2+x3+x4, data = dat2wayRC))

head(dat2wayRC)

model2 <- "
f1 =~ x1 + x2 + x3
f2 =~ x4
f12 =~ x1x4o + x2x4o + x3x4o
f3 =~ x7 + x8 + x9
f3 ~ f1 + f2 + f12
"

fitRC2way2 <- sem(model2, data = dat2wayRC, std.lv = FALSE,
                 meanstructure = TRUE)
summary(fitRC2way2)

messages.author: bec3b6c763e426c0
messages.subject: Re: Looking under the hood of the indProd function
parts: Alex: thanks for probing into this. Indeed, it's strange that the manual and orthgonalized methods produce similar product terms (and regression estimates) for the semTools dataset (and for my dataset when I have three indicators measuring each main effect), but that the results are different for my dataset with a single indicator for one of the main effect variables. I wouldn't have expected that the nature of the data set (correlations and centering) would affect the simple production of the product terms for numeric variables.
